content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: delay payments breaks, move 4 cross-skilled agents to payments and turn on IVR callback, at no extra cost, for a predicted 87.3% service level against the 80% target.","why":"Payments demand spiked because of the UPI outage (P1 incident INC-20261027-4076). 'UPI payment failed' calls are at 154 against 68.8 expected, and service level fell to 2.5% at 13:30. This is not a staffing problem. For the disruption window (14:30-16:30), even doing nothing is predicted to reach 86.6% (payments 83.0%). P1 lifts that to 87.3% (payments 84.1%) and cuts abandons from 3.0% to 2.6% at zero cost. It is the cheapest policy-compliant plan that meets the target. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 90.6%.","trade_offs":["Cost: P1 costs nothing. P4 (cancel coaching, move 6 agents) reaches the best result, 87.8% with 2.5% abandons, but costs INR 450 and loses general coaching. P3 costs INR 588, uses the last overtime budget and does slightly worse (87.1%).","Customer impact: P1 improves payments abandons from 3.0% to 2.6% compared with no action. P2 costs INR 228 and predicts 86.3%, which is worse than doing nothing.","Other queue: moving 4 agents drops general only slightly, from 94.5% to 94.3%, still well above target.","Staff: payments agents' breaks are pushed back 45 minutes between 15:00 and 16:00."],"watch":"Watch payments volume against the UPI incident status. If the outage lasts beyond 16:00 or calls keep rising past the 201 seen at 13:30, consider P4 next. Overtime (P3) would use the last of the budget, so treat it as a last resort. No escalation to the duty manager is needed."}
